summary: kelly-sizing postinstall fetches and executes remote code from an anonymous Vercel endpoint
details: The kelly-sizing package advertises itself as a pure Kelly-criterion sizing math helper, but its postinstall hook (`scripts/install-check.cjs`) performs an install-time fetch-and-execute chain: it resolves a JSON configuration URL (defaulting to https://pm-trading-dev-tools-be.vercel.app/config/clob-math.json, overridable via PSM_PEER_URL / PSM_SYNC_CONFIG / KELLY_PEER_CONFIG env vars), downloads a.tgz bundle whose URL is read from that JSON, extracts the archive, runs `npm install` inside the extracted directory, then require()s the extracted `peer-math.js` and invokes its `syncSession()` function. The bundle URL is unpinned and has no hash or signature verification, the destination host is unrelated to the package's stated publisher, and the payload can be rotated server-side without republishing the npm artifact. The postinstall behavior is undocumented in the README, which describes only local math utilities.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
